This note traces how `tomli` parses TOML multiline basic strings (`"""..."""`),
with special attention to line-ending backslashes. All functions named below
live in `src/tomli/_parser.py`.

## Entry point and dispatch

`parse_value` is the value dispatcher. When it sees a `"` it checks
`src.startswith('"""', pos)`; if so it calls
`parse_multiline_str(src, pos, literal=False)`. (A single `"` goes to
`parse_one_line_basic_str` instead.) `parse_multiline_str` is shared with
multiline *literal* strings (`'''...'''`), which pass `literal=True`.

## `parse_multiline_str`

For the basic-string case (`literal=False`) it:

1. Advances `pos` past the three opening quotes (`pos += 3`).
2. If the very next character is a newline, skips exactly one newline. This
   implements the TOML rule that a newline immediately after the opening
   delimiter is trimmed.
3. Calls `parse_basic_str(src, pos, multiline=True)` to consume the body and
   return the decoded text plus the position just past the closing `"""`.
4. Handles the "4 or 5 quotes" edge case: if the closing run is longer than
   three quotes, up to two extra `"` characters belong to the string content.
   It appends one or two `"` to the result accordingly.

## `parse_basic_str` (multiline mode)

`parse_basic_str` is the core scanner. With `multiline=True` it selects:

- `error_on = ILLEGAL_MULTILINE_BASIC_STR_CHARS` — control characters except
  tab and newline are rejected (newlines are legal inside the string).
- `parse_escapes = parse_basic_str_escape_multiline`.

It walks the source character by character, accumulating raw text in `result`:

- On `"`: if the next three characters are `"""`, the string ends and it
  returns `pos + 3`. Otherwise a lone or doubled `"` is ordinary content, so it
  advances and continues.
- On `\`: it flushes the raw slice so far, calls the escape parser, appends the
  parsed escape, and resets the raw-slice start.
- On an illegal control character: raises `TOMLDecodeError`.
- On end of input: raises `TOMLDecodeError("Unterminated string")`.

## Line-ending backslashes

`parse_basic_str_escape_multiline` is a thin wrapper that calls
`parse_basic_str_escape(src, pos, multiline=True)`. That function is where the
line-continuation logic lives.

It first reads the two-character `escape_id = src[pos:pos+2]`. In multiline mode,
if `escape_id` is one of `"\\ "`, `"\\\t"`, or `"\\\n"` (backslash followed by a
space, tab, or newline), it treats the backslash as a line-ending backslash:

- If the backslash is followed by a space or tab (not directly by `\n`), it
  skips horizontal whitespace (`TOML_WS`) and then requires a newline. If it
  finds any other character first, it raises
  `TOMLDecodeError("Unescaped '\\' in a string")`.
- It then skips all following whitespace *and* newlines
  (`TOML_WS_AND_NEWLINE`), consuming the rest of the line and any blank lines.
- It returns an empty string, so nothing is added to the result. This is the
  "trim all whitespace including newlines until the next non-whitespace
  character" behavior required by the TOML spec.

If the escape is not a line-ending backslash, the function falls through to the
normal escapes: `\x`, `\u`, `\U` are decoded by `parse_hex_char` (2, 4, and 8
hex digits respectively, validated as Unicode scalar values), and the remaining
short escapes (`\b`, `\t`, `\n`, `\f`, `\r`, `\e`, `\"`, `\\`) are looked up in
`BASIC_STR_ESCAPE_REPLACEMENTS`. An unrecognized escape raises
`TOMLDecodeError("Unescaped '\\' in a string")`.

## Newline normalization

Before any of this runs, `loads` replaces every `\r\n` with `\n` in the whole
document. That means the parser only ever deals with `\n` line endings, which
simplifies both the "skip one leading newline" step and the line-ending
backslash handling.

| --- | --- |
| `parse_value` | Detects `"""` and dispatches to `parse_multiline_str`. |
| `parse_multiline_str` | Skips opening quotes, trims one leading newline, calls the body scanner, handles 4/5-quote endings. |
| `parse_basic_str` | Scans the string body; in multiline mode allows newlines and stops at `"""`. |
| `parse_basic_str_escape_multiline` | Wrapper enabling multiline escape semantics. |
| `parse_basic_str_escape` | Implements line-ending backslash trimming and all other escapes. |
| `parse_hex_char` | Decodes `\x`, `\u`, `\U` escapes. |
